content.text:
Not being able to fully empty your bladder is called **urinary retention**. It can happen because urine is **blocked from leaving**, the bladder muscle is **too weak to squeeze well**, or the nerves/signals that coordinate urination aren’t working normally. ([niddk.nih.gov](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/urinary-retention/symptoms-causes?utm_source=openai))

Common causes include:

- **Enlarged prostate** in men, which can squeeze the urethra and block urine flow.
- **Urethral blockage or narrowing**, such as scar tissue/stricture, stones, tumors, or severe constipation pressing on the urinary tract.
- **Urinary tract infection or inflammation**, which can cause swelling and make it hard to pass urine.
- **Medication side effects**, especially some antihistamines, decongestants, antidepressants, muscle relaxers, opioids, and bladder-control medicines.
- **Nerve problems** from diabetes, stroke, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s disease, spinal cord injury, pelvic surgery, or anesthesia.
- **Weak or underactive bladder muscle**, sometimes from aging, long-term overdistension, nerve damage, or chronic obstruction.
- **Pelvic organ prolapse** in women, where pelvic organs press on or kink the urinary pathway.
- **Constipation**, which can physically interfere with bladder emptying. ([niddk.nih.gov](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/urinary-retention/symptoms-causes?utm_source=openai))

**Seek urgent medical care now** if you **cannot urinate at all**, have severe lower belly pain/swelling, fever, back/flank pain, vomiting, confusion, or blood in the urine. Acute urinary retention can be an emergency because pressure can back up and harm the bladder or kidneys. ([niddk.nih.gov](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/urinary-retention/symptoms-causes?utm_source=openai))

If this is ongoing but you can still urinate, it’s still worth scheduling a visit soon. A clinician can check for retained urine after you pee, test for infection, review medications, and look for prostate, pelvic, nerve, or blockage-related causes.
